DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.claim: Ḥamīm can mean a close relative or intimate friend.
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.anchor: فوجه منهما : الحميم القريب قوله تعالى في سورة المعارج

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.claim: The passage depicts cosmic upheaval and the collapse of social bonds; each person would offer even close family and tribe as ransom, while Hell burns and seizes those who evaded the call and hoarded wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.anchor: The flames of Hell shall tear and burn his skin

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r3.claim: They read لا يسأل actively: a close friend does not seek help or benefit from another, knowing none is available.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ولا يسئل مبنيا للفاعل، أي لا يسأله نصرة ولا منفعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r4.claim: He says a close friend is not asked about his condition because it is plain; other explanations say he is not asked to bear sins or intercede.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا يسأله عن حاله لأنها ظاهرة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r5.speaker: أبو حيوة وشيبة وأبو جعفر والبزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r5.claim: They read the verb passively: no one is asked to summon a close friend, or to bear that friend's sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وشيبة وأبو جعفر والبزي: بخلاف عن ثلاثتهم مبنيا للمفعول

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r4.claim: They are shown to one another amid such terror that they cannot ask each other's condition, let alone search farther away.
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r4.anchor: öyle bir dehşet ki birbirlerine gösterilip dururlarken bile soramaz, nerede kaldı ki uzağı arasın

FARRA:v3p183#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p183#2/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p183#2/r8.claim: A close relative will not ask about another relative; they recognize one another for an hour, then recognition ends.
FARRA:v3p183#2/r8.anchor: لا يسأل ذو قرابة عن قرابته

FARRA:v3p183#2/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p183#2/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p183#2/r9.claim: Some read the clause passively, meaning no one asks a person where his close relative is; Farrāʾ dislikes it because it conflicts with the explanation and the readers agree on the active form.
FARRA:v3p183#2/r9.anchor: وقد قرأ بعضهم: (ولا يسأل حميم حميما ) لا يقال لحميم : أين حميمك؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.claim: Another interpretation of the statement that no intimate asks about an intimate is that no one is questioned about his sin and deeds to be held accountable for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.anchor: وقيل المعنى: لا يسأل عن ذنبه وأعماله ليؤخذ بها وليزر وزره

TABRISI:70:1-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:1-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:1-10/r10.claim: On the passive reading, no close friend asks about his friend to discover his condition as friends and relatives ordinarily do.
TABRISI:70:1-10/r10.anchor: المعنى والله أعلم لا يسئل حميم عن حميمه ليعرف شأنه من جهته كما يتعرف الخبر الصديق من جهة صديقه والقريب عن قريبه

TABRISI:70:1-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:1-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:1-10/r11.claim: When the verb is made passive after deleting the preposition, its former object of the preposition appears as the accusative حميما.
TABRISI:70:1-10/r11.anchor: وقد يحذف الجار فيصل الفعل إلى الاسم الذي كان مجرورا قبل حذف الجار فينتصب بأنه مفعول الاسم الذي أسند إليه الفعل المبني للمفعول به فعلى هذا انتصب قوله حميما

TABRISI:70:1-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:1-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:1-10/r12.claim: The phrase “they see them” supports this reading: once friends see one another, they need not ask about one another.
TABRISI:70:1-10/r12.anchor: أي يبصر الحميم الحميم تقول بصرت به

TABRISI:70:1-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:1-10/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:1-10/r13.claim: The verb's transitive construction shifts the object when the preposition is omitted; plural wording reflects many intimates despite singular حميم.
TABRISI:70:1-10/r13.anchor: فإذا بصروهم لم يحتج إلى تعرف شأن الحميم من حميمه

STUDYQURAN:70:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:10/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:70:10/r1.claim: Judgment and Resurrection overwhelm people so completely that each is concerned only for himself, even disregarding his closest companions.
STUDYQURAN:70:10/r1.anchor: The Day of Judgment and the Resurrection will be so overwhelming that people will have no concern for anyone except themselves, even for their most loyal companions in earthly life

TABATABAI:70:5-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:5-11/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:5-11/r9.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative whose affairs one cares about; the verse shows the Day’s severity, since each person is so occupied with himself that even close kin do not ask after one another.
TABATABAI:70:5-11/r9.anchor: الحميم القريب الذي تهتم بأمره وتشفق عليه. إشارة إلى شدة اليوم فالإنسان يومئذ

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.claim: The passage escalates beyond intimates not asking after one another: the criminal would ransom himself with increasingly precious relatives, then everyone on earth, if that could save him.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r9.anchor: وسياق هذه الآيات سياق الإضراب والترقي بالنسبة إلى قوله { ولا يسأل حميم حميما } فيفيد

BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r6.claim: No close friend or relative asks another about their condition or speaks to them, because each is occupied by their own ordeal; if relatives do not, strangers certainly will not.
BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r6.anchor: أي لا يسأل قريب قريبا عن أحواله ولا يكلمه لابتلاء كل منهم بما شغله عن ذلك

BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r7.claim: The indefinite wording generalizes the scene to every close-friend pair.
BURSEVI:v10p121#2/r7.anchor: وإذا كان الحال بين الأقارب هكذا فكيف يكون بين الأجانب والتنكير للتعميم

TABRISI:70:10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:10/r1.claim: The verse is set beside the plea for no intercessors or close friend in 26:101.
TABRISI:70:10/r1.anchor: فما لنا من شافعين ولا صديق حميم

TABRISI:70:10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:10/r2.claim: No close friend asks after another on that Day because each is absorbed in his own affair, as in 80:37.
TABRISI:70:10/r2.anchor: لا يسأل الحميم عن حميمه في ذلك اليوم لأنه يذهب عن ذلك

TABRISI:70:10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:10/r7.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative, from the sense of nearness; the cited poetry uses it in this sense.

TABRISI:70:10#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10#2/r17.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:70:10#2/r17.claim: Mujahid says everyone is so occupied with himself that no close friend asks after another.
TABRISI:70:10#2/r17.anchor: لشغل كل إنسان بنفسه عن غيره عن مجاهد

TABRISI:70:10#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10#2/r18.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:70:10#2/r18.claim: Al-Hasan says one close friend does not ask another to carry his sins because he has despaired of that help in the afterlife.
TABRISI:70:10#2/r18.anchor: لا يسأل حميم حميما أن يتحمل عنه من أوزاره ليأسه منه ذلك في الآخرة عن الحسن

TABRISI:70:10#2/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10#2/r19.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:70:10#2/r19.claim: Al-Akhfash defines a ḥamīm as someone specially loved, related by blood or not; al-ḥāmah means one’s close circle.
TABRISI:70:10#2/r19.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الحميم من يخصه الرجل مودة وشفقة من قريب الرحم وبعيده

TABRISI:70:10#2/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:10#2/r20.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:70:10#2/r20.claim: Another explanation says no one needs to ask, since people are recognizable by signs: disbelievers’ faces are black and eyes blue, while believers’ color is radiant and faces white.
TABRISI:70:10#2/r20.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه لا يحتاج إلى سؤاله لأنه يكون لكل علامة يعرف بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r1.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative for whom one feels protective anger and who feels it for you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الحميم: القريب الذي تغضب له ويغضب لك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r2.claim: No relative asks after another because each is absorbed in himself; the verse parallels the mother who forgets her nursling and a person fleeing his brother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r2.anchor: والمعنى: لا يسأل الحميم عن حميمه في ذلك اليوم؛ لأنه يذهل عن ذلك ويشتغل عنه بشأنه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r3.claim: Muqatil says a man does not ask after his relatives because of the terrors of that day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول لا يسأل الرجل قرابته من شدة الأهوال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r4.claim: The active form can mean asking Zayd about his state or affairs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r4.anchor: من قولك: سألت زيدا، أي: سألته عن حاله وأمره.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r5.claim: Alternatively, it can mean that he does not ask about his relative, with the preposition omitted and the verb made transitive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: لا يسأل عن حميمه، فيحذف الجار، ويوصل الفعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the verb passively: one relative is not asked about another in order to learn his condition from him; this too omits the preposition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن كثير: {ولا يسأل} بضم الياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r7.claim: Al-Farra paraphrases it as no one asking a friend where his friend is, but dislikes the passive reading because it conflicts with the exegesis and readers’ consensus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p213/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: أي لا يقال لحميم: أين حميمك؟ قال: ولست أشتهي ضم الياء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r5.claim: No close relative asks about another because each is preoccupied with his own ordeal.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:70:8-13/r5.anchor: لا يسأل قريب عن قريب لاشتغاله بما هو فيه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.claim: The sinner's psychological terror is so intense that he would sacrifice his spouse, children, closest relatives and loved ones, and even everyone on earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r3.anchor: insanın âkıbetinden sarsıcı bir kesit verilmektedir. Buna rağmen o gün suçlu kişinin, en değerli varlıkları olan eşini, çocuklarını ve diğer yakınlarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.claim: Exegetes say the “sinner” whose state is described can mean unbelievers or, more generally, sinners.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r4.anchor: Müfessirler, burada ruh hali tasvir edilen “mücrim”in (suçlu) inkârcıları veya daha genel olarak günahkârları ifade ettiğini belirtirler

BURHAN:v4p164/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p164/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p164/r1.claim: سأل can take two objects like أعطى, though either object may be left unexpressed.
BURHAN:v4p164/r1.anchor: تتعدى لمفعوليين كأعطى ويجوز الاقتصار على أحدهما

BURHAN:v4p164/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p164/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p164/r4.claim: One two-object pattern makes سأل equivalent to أعطى: asking someone for a thing or asking them to do it.
BURHAN:v4p164/r4.anchor: أحدها إن تكون بمنزلة أعطيت كقولك سألت زيدا بعد عمرو حقا أي استعطيته أو سألته أن يفعل ذلك

BURHAN:v4p164/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p164/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p164/r5.claim: Another pattern makes it equivalent to selecting someone from a group; here it means no intimate asks about an intimate because each is too distracted to think of the other.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r1.claim: Ḥamīm means hot water; ḥamiyya is hot anger or jealousy, and ḥamīm can also mean a close relative.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r1.anchor: الحميم : الماء الحار . والحمية : حرارة الغضب والغيرة . ويقال : الحميم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p236/r3.claim: Ḥamīm can mean a close blood relative.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#6/r1.claim: No close relative asks after another relative; though they see them, they recognize them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#6/r1.anchor: {ولا يسأل حميم حميما} أي لا يسأل ذو قرابة عن قرابته؛ ولكنهم {يبصرونهم} أي يعرفونهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#7/r1.claim: No close relative asks after another relative; though they see them, they recognize them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p485#7/r1.anchor: {ولا يسأل حميم حميما} أي لا يسأل ذو قرابة عن قرابته؛ ولكنهم {يبصرونهم} أي يعرفونهم

MAJAZ:v2p269/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r1.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative or intimate.

ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r6.claim: A reading omits the second ḥamīman, while another includes it; their different syntax yields different interpretations.
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r6.anchor: وقرئت (ولا يسأل حميم). فمن قرأ (ولا يسأل) فالمعنى أنهم يعرف بعضهم بعضا

ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r7.claim: Without the second ḥamīm, the meaning is that close associates recognize one another, supported by the statement that they see one another.
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r7.anchor: فمن قرأ (ولا يسأل) فالمعنى أنهم يعرف بعضهم بعضا، ويدل عليه قوله: (يبصرونهم)

ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r8.claim: With the second ḥamīm, the meaning is that no relative asks about a relative; Zajjāj suggests that the ones being seen are angels.
ZAJJAJ:v5p220/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ (ولا يسأل حميم حميما). فالمعنى لا يسأل قريب عن قرابته

ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r4.claim: No friend will ask about a friend on that Day, even though they can see one another.
ASAD-NOTES:70:5/r4.anchor: no friend will ask about his friend

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r1.claim: For the preceding term, al-Rāghib interprets the fire’s subsiding as its flame becoming still, while al-Qurṭubī clarifies that this does not lessen pain or punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r1.anchor: وفسرها "الراغب" بسكون لهبها، كأنه صار عليها خباء من رماد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p510/r4.claim: The al-Maʿārij citation continues from the image of the sky like muhl to the next verse, where no close friend asks after another.

QIRAAT-ER:70:10:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:70:10:3#1/r1.speaker: Pss
QIRAAT-ER:70:10:3#1/r1.claim: Pss reads the verb passively: no intimate is asked about an intimate. This shifts the sense from active refusal to passive impossibility; the reading is attributed to some of the Ten.
QIRAAT-ER:70:10:3#1/r1.anchor: Pss, mutawatir: "Passive voice: ""no intimate is asked about an intimate""

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says no compassionate close relative asks another about his condition or speaks to him, since each is absorbed in what occupies him; Al-Ālūsī finds this the most terrifying explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r1.anchor: أي لا يسأل قريب مشفق قريبا مشفقا عن حاله ولا يكلمه لابتلاء كل منهم بما يشغله عن ذلك أخرجه ابن المنذر وعبد بن حميد عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r2.claim: In another report, Qatāda says a relative does not ask about the other’s state because it is plain to see.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r2.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه لا يسأله عن حاله لأنها ظاهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r3.claim: Another view says no relative asks another to carry any of his sins, since he has despaired of that help.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r3.anchor: وقيل لا يسأله أن يحمل عنه من أوزاره شيئا ليأسه عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r4.claim: Another view says no relative asks another for intercession.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r5.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r5.claim: Al-Baḥr says relatives do not ask one another for help or benefit, knowing they will receive none; Al-Ālūsī prefers Qatāda’s first, more alarming sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r5.anchor: في البحر لا يسأله نصره ولا منفعته لعلمه أنه لا يجد ذلك عنده ولعل الأول أبلغ في التهويل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r6.claim: The second object of yasʾalu is omitted; alternatively, ḥamīman is construed with an elided preposition, “about a close relative.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r6.anchor: وأيا ما كان فمفعول يسأل الثاني محذوف وقيل حميما منصوب بنزع الخافض أي لا يسأل حميم عن حميم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة وشيبة وأبو جعفر والبزي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r7.claim: These readers, with disagreement reported for some, read the verb passively: no relative is asked for, summoned, or questioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وشيبة وأبو جعفر والبزي بخلاف عن ثلاثتهم ولا يسأل مبنيا للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r8.claim: With the passive reading, one explanation is that a close relative is not asked to come or provide help; another is that his condition is not asked.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r8.anchor: أي لا يطلب من حميم حميم ولا يكلف إحضاره أو لا يسأل منه حاله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r9.claim: A further explanation of the passive reading is that no one asks for a relative’s sins to be taken on himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p59#3/r9.anchor: وقيل لا يسأل ذنوب جميمه ليؤخذ بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r1.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r1.claim: Al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir reads yusʾalu passively: no close relative is asked about another, such as where the relative is.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r1.anchor: قرأ البزي عن ابن كثير "لا يسأل" بضم الياء أي: لا يسأل حميم عن حميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r2.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r2.claim: Other readers use the active form: a close relative does not ask after another because each is occupied with himself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r2.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بفتح الياء، أي: لا يسأل قريب قريبا لشغله بشأن نفسه.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r1.claim: On the active reading, close friends and relatives ask nothing because of overwhelming distraction and the disclosure that no soul can help another; kinship ties have dissolved and only piety matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r1.anchor: من شدة الأهوال { حميم حميما } أي قريب في غاية القرب والصداقة قريبا مثله عن شيء من الأشياء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r2.claim: The majority read the verb actively: one close person does not ask another about anything.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r2.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بفتح الياء وعلى قراءة ابن كثير بالبناء للمفعول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the verb passively: no one is asked to answer for another, unlike worldly rulers who may hold a favored person’s relatives responsible; God's power encompasses all equally.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r3.anchor: وعلى قراءة ابن كثير بالبناء للمفعول المعنى أنه لا يطالب أحد بأحد كما بعض الحكام في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r4.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r4.claim: Al-Baghawī says every creature at the Resurrection, human or jinn, is in view of its companion.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r4.anchor: قال البغوي : وليس في القيامة مخلوق إلا وهو نصب عين صاحبه من الجن والإنس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r5.claim: People see one another, so the lack of questions is not due to concealment; each is absorbed in personal concerns and flees from the other.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p147/r5.anchor: فعدم السؤال لا للخفاء بل للاشتغال وهم كل إنسان بما عنده

DURR-FULL:v8p280/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p280/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p280/r11.claim: Qatada says each person will be so occupied with himself that he will not ask after others.
DURR-FULL:v8p280/r11.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولا يسأل حميم حميما} قال: شغل كل إنسان بنفسه عن الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r5.claim: If “the day when the sky…” opens a new sentence, it is an embedded-subject substitute for the no-question statement: terror causes the failure to ask, and the criminal’s wish to ransom is part of that scene.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r5.anchor: لأن عدم المساءلة مسبب عن شدة الهول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r14.claim: Friends do not ask after each other because terror leaves each occupied with his own distress, even while he sees his close friend suffering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r14.anchor: فمن شدة ذلك أن يرى الحميم حميمه في كرب وعناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r15.claim: The object of “ask” is omitted because its meaning—asking about the friend’s condition—is clear from context and from their seeing one another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p158/r15.anchor: أي يبصر الأخلاء أحوال أخلائهم من الكرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r16.speaker: السبعة والحسن والمدنيون وطلحة والناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r16.claim: The seven readers, al-Hasan, the Medinans, Talha, and others read ولا يسأل actively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r16.anchor: وقرأ السبعة والحسن والمدنيون وطلحة والناس: «ولا يسأل» على بناء الفعل للفاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r17.claim: Here a hamim is a close relative or ally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r17.anchor: والحميم في هذا الموضع: القريب والوالي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r18.claim: A close one is not asked for help or benefit because the person knows none is available.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r18.anchor: والمعنى لا يسأله نصرة ولا منفعة لعلمه أنه لا يجدها عنده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r19.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r19.claim: Qatada says no one asks about another’s condition because everyone can see it and is occupied with himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r19.anchor: قال قتادة: المعنى لا يسأله عن حاله لأنها ظاهرة قد بصر كل أحد حالة الجميع، وشغل بنفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r20.speaker: ابن كثير والبزي وأبو جعفر وشيبة وأبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r20.claim: Ibn Kathir through al-Bazzi, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba in a differing transmission, and Abu Haywa read لا يسأل passively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r20.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير من طريق البزي وأبو جعفر وشيبة بخلاف عنهما وأبو حيوة «لا يسأل» على بناء الفعل للمفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r21.claim: On the passive reading, no one is asked to appear; every criminal is identifiable by a mark, as every believer bears a mark of goodness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366/r21.anchor: فالمعنى: ولا يسأل إحضاره لأن كل مجرم له سيما يعرف بها، وكذلك كل مؤمن له سيما خير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r1.claim: The majority read the verb actively: one close friend does not ask about another, being preoccupied with himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r1.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون سأل بفتح الياء والمعنى لا يسأل قريب عن قرابته لاشتغاله بنفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r2.claim: On the active reading, a man neither asks about nor speaks to his kin because of the terrors.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل لا يسأل الرجل قرابته ولا يكلمه من شدة الأهوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r3.speaker: معاوية، أبو رزين، الحسن، سعيد بن جبير، مجاهد، عكرمة، ابن محيصن، ابن أبي عبلة، أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r3.claim: They read the verb passively with ḍamma on yāʾ: no one asks the close friend where his friend is.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361/r3.anchor: وقرأ معاوية وأبو رزين والحسن وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعكرمة وابن محيصن وابن أبي عبلة وأبو جعفر بضم الياء والمعنى لا يقال للحميم أين حميمك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r3.claim: A close relative does not ask about another's condition despite seeing him in the worst state, because each person is occupied with himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r3.anchor: أي: لا يسأل القريب عن حاله، وهو يراه في أسوأ الأحوال، فتشغله نفسه عن غيره.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن العوفي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r4.claim: Al-ʿAwfi reports Ibn Abbas saying that people recognize one another, then flee from one another because each has enough to occupy him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: يعرف بعضهم بعضا، ويتعارفون بينهم، ثم يفر بعضهم من بعض بعد ذلك، يقول: {لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir connects the scene to verses saying kin cannot bear another's burden, there will be no kinship or questioning, and people flee their closest family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p224#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية الكريمة كقوله: {يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم واخشوا يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده

JISHUMI:v10p7077/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r1.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير، والبرجمي عن عاصم، والحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r1.claim: These readers use ḍamma on yāʾ: an intimate is not asked about another.
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r1.anchor: قرأ البزي عن ابن كثير، والبرجمي عن عاصم: ولا يسأل بضم الياء، أي: لا يسأل حميم عن حميم،

JISHUMI:v10p7077/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r2.speaker: القراء
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r2.claim: Most readers use fatḥa: no one asks another because each is occupied with himself.
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r2.anchor: والقراء على فتح الياء، أي: لا يسأل أحد أحدا لشغله بنفسه.

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r4.claim: Ḥamīman is object of saʾala; alternatively it means “about an intimate,” with the preposition omitted.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r4.anchor: حميما نصب ب (سأل)، وقيل: معناه: عن حميم، فلما حذف الخافض نصب.

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r10.claim: An intimate does not ask after another because each is absorbed in himself.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r10.anchor: أي: قريب قريبا شيئا لشغل كل إنسان بنفسه عن غيره، عن قتادة،

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r11.claim: Another view says no one asks an intimate’s state, since everyone recognizes it from features.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r11.anchor: وقيل: لا يسأل حميم حميما ليعرف حاله؛ لأن كل أحد يعرف بسيماه،

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r12.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says no one asks another to carry sins, despairing of that in the next life.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r12.anchor: وقيل: لا يسأل أن يحتمل عنه شيئا من أوزاره ليأسه من ذلك في الآخرة، عن الحسن.

MUQATIL:70:8-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r3.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative; the terrified man neither asks after nor speaks to his kin.
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r3.anchor: { ولا يسأل حميم حميما } [آية: 10] يعني قريب قريبا، يقولك لا يسأل الرجل قرابته، ولا يكلمه من شدة الأهوال

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r1.claim: No close relative asks about another because each is occupied with himself.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r1.anchor: لا يسأل قريب عن قريب لاشتغاله بنفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r2.speaker: البزي والبرجمي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r2.claim: Al-Bazzī and al-Barjamī read the verb with ḍamma on the yāʾ: one relative is not asked about another or held accountable for the other's sin.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279/r2.anchor: وعن البزي والبرجمي بضم الياء أي لا يسأل قريب عن قريب أي لا يطالب به

QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r11.claim: Qatada says no close friend asks about another's condition because each is absorbed in himself, as in 80:37.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r11.anchor: { ولا يسأل حميم حميما } أي عن شأنه لشغل كل إنسان بنفسه، قاله قتادة. كما قال تعالى: لكل امرىء منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه

QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r12.claim: Another syntax supplies an omitted preposition: no close friend is asked about another close friend.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r12.anchor: وقيل: لا يسأل حميم عن حميم، فحذف الجار ووصل الفعل.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r13.speaker: شيبة والبزي عن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r13.claim: The general reading has active yasʾalu with fatḥa on yāʾ; Shayba and al-Bazzi from Asim read passive yusʾalu with ḍamma, meaning relatives are not questioned about each other, since everyone is answerable for their deeds, as in 74:38.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:8-10/r13.anchor: وقراءة العامة «يسأل» بفتح الياء. وقرأ شيبة والبزي عن عاصم «ولا يسأل» بالضم على ما لم يسم فاعله
